The corrupted element is most likely **M2**, the PMOS current-source load, whose multiplier appears to be m=3 instead of m=1.

M2 is in triode (Vds = 0.058 V < Vdsat = 0.199 V), which pulls vout up to 1.742 V, near VDD. The reference M3 (W/L ≈ 5.1, 9.9 µA) sets Vsg ≈ 1.127 V. M2 at m=3 has an effective W/L of about 305, roughly 60× the reference. That mirror ratio would demand about 590 µA, far more than the 181 µA the NMOS M1 can sink, so M2 is overdriven and drops into triode. With m=1 the effective W/L is about 102, a ratio of about 20×, which gives roughly 180–200 µA and matches the 181 µA that M1 actually carries. The sensitivities agree: increasing M2 lowers gain and raises vout_dc, both consistent with an oversized current source.
